replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body:
No. The focus of the update seems to be on adding more ways for you to control the output of the image, as well as consistency.

The consistency is the best part here. Providing an image and not having it subtly shift 52 pixels and change ratios slightly is fucking huge for adding it to a workflow.  This is massive for giving us more of a ControlNet style capacity here. Also  claims to be able to do things like rotate perspectives more consistently. Soooo we're looking at better reference pose sheets. Might help people make isometric assets easier. Dunno. I'm going to try running some of my character scribbles through and see if it can give me consistent anatomy. I'll be really impressed if so, as it tended to do a very poor job interpreting 3/4 and side profiles before.

replies.author: odragora
replies.body: Maybe it also makes it much better for creating animated sprites, without having individual frames losing their precise position.

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: Supposedly Astra does well with aseprite, but that program has a reliable onion skinning for the model to work with and see the before/after pose, helping it create a good sprite sheet. I don't have much confidence in GPT Images 2.5 doing the same unless it can like create them one at a time with the previous image as its own reference in a single workflow. Maybe it can though.

replies.author: FailedGradAdmissions
replies.body:
No, but it's game changing editing an sprite you already have and keeping consistency. Just a few days ago I was working with some sprites and it was terrible as every edit always changed something else. For humanoids if I asked to change hairstyle it slightly changed the face, clothes sometimes even the limbs. Now it just works.

Very unethical but we are at the point where you couod go search for a sprite and then tell gpt to change it to your taste.

comments.author: AustinMHowe
comments.body:
It’s very good and much better with instruction.

Context: Sensipets has a layer-based clothing system.   
It’s been a struggle to design an effective system and know what to prompt + send as reference images. After an evening with Astra-high there are some very promising results for a very complex task. Still some work to do with cuffs/layer splitting but much better results than Astra-high with 2 (with recent transparency update)
